subject: fashion-design
intro: Fashion design leads into the studios, workrooms and buying floors of the garment trade — the people who invent the clothes, cut the patterns that build them, sew them, and choose what reaches the shops.

roles.title: Fashion Designers
roles.what: Design clothing and accessories, creating original designs or adapting fashion trends into lines and collections that factories can actually make and customers will buy.
roles.where: The whole arc of the course feeds this role: research books and concept development from unit 1, fashion drawing and flats from unit 2, and the collection line-ups and styling of unit 5 become the job itself.

roles.title: Wholesale and Retail Buyers, Except Farm Products
roles.what: Buy the merchandise a retailer or wholesaler will resell: study what sells, attend markets and showrooms, negotiate prices and terms, and plan the ranges that fill the stores each season.
roles.where: Unit 6's brand, buying and merchandising topics are the core of the job, backed by unit 4's fibre and fabric knowledge — the vocabulary buyers need when judging a garment and its price point.

roles.title: Tailors, Dressmakers, and Custom Sewers
roles.what: Design, make, alter, repair and fit garments one client at a time — measuring, marking and sewing cloth so that a made-to-measure piece sits exactly right on the body.
roles.where: Unit 3's pattern cutting and construction is the craft here: block patterns and dart manipulation, draping on the stand, and the toile, fit and finishing cycle used for every custom garment.
